findings.message: <video> with data-start is nested inside <div id="s6"> which also has data-start. The frame extractor resolves the video's start from its own data-start without the wrapper's offset, while visibility uses the wrapper's window, so the two disagree: the clip shows the wrong source frames and then disappears partway through its slot.
findings.fixHint: A <video> takes no timing from its wrapper: time the <video> and leave the wrapper untimed (remove its data-start; it only places or animates), or move the <video> up to be a direct child of the stage.

findings.message: 2 tl.fromTo() calls target "#imlec" with no stable baseline. The last-authored fromTo "from" values become the element's resting state for any seek before the first tween actually runs, because GSAP applies fromTo from-values at authoring time (immediateRender), not at tween position.
findings.fixHint: Add `immediateRender: false` to every fromTo except the earliest-positioned one (at 13.2s), so pre-first-tween seeks keep its "from" values. A hiding `tl.set(..., 0)` baseline trips gsap_timeline_set_initial_hide, and a `gsap.set` authored before the fromTo calls is overwritten by them.

findings.message: <path> is hidden with stroke-dasharray 1 and stroke-dashoffset 1 on pathLength 1, but its round cap can still paint a dot at the end of the path (Chrome rounds the zero-length dash differently per curve).
findings.fixHint: Make the gap longer than the path (stroke-dasharray "1 1.2" with stroke-dashoffset 1.1), or keep the element visibility:hidden until its draw tween starts.

findings.message: In timeline "main", a tween on scale, opacity of #tel-sahne ends at 8.800 s, 0.050 s after a later tween on scale, opacity ends at 8.750 s. For that tail the earlier tween takes scale, opacity back and leaves its own end value on screen, so the later tween's end never shows. End the earlier tween by 8.300 s, or add overwrite: "auto" to the later tween.
